findings.claim: The assessment does not actually assess the current typed-mutation/control-plane implementation required by the KBD goal.
findings.evidence: Goal requires: "Repair canonical KBD project identity initialization and prove typed mutations work". The KBD assessment covers manifest identity, daemon focus, and legacy migration, then only states a desired end condition: "a typed command commits through the control plane and replays after restart". There is no finding identifying the current typed-command API, journal/control-plane path, replay mechanism, or whether it is present, broken, or untested.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a concrete gap analysis for typed mutations: identify the relevant KBD command/control-plane/journal/replay files or service endpoints, state their current behavior, and specify what is missing or failing before planning initialization proof work.

findings.claim: The UAR assessment relies on external source and workflow paths that are absent from the provided repository tree without clearly separating what downstream work can verify in this repo versus external worktrees.
findings.evidence: The assessment claims repairs in "src/bin/uar-sidecar.rs", "src/server.rs", and ".github/workflows/publish-ghcr.yml", but the packet's cited paths report: "MISSING  publish-ghcr.yml" and "MISSING  src/bin/uar-sidecar.rs"; the only "src/server.rs" matches are BossFang crate paths: "crates/librefang-acp/src/server.rs, crates/librefang-api/src/server.rs, crates/librefang-desktop/src/server.rs".
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit external-repository section naming the UAR repository/worktree and exact paths there, and separately list BossFang-local paths that must change, so the plan does not target missing or wrong in-repo files.
